mainTopic: The extra דינר needed for כתובת בנין דכרין: what counts toward it, and when it is measured
overview: A ברייתא has the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון both requiring one extra דינר beyond the two כתובות before sons can collect their mothers' כתובות, and the גמרא looks for the real difference between them. It tries movables versus land, then free versus liened land, then less than a דינר. Each attempt is challenged. It finally returns to the first two ideas with the opinions reversed, so רבי שמעון is the strict one. מר זוטרא then rules that when one wife died in the husband's lifetime and one after his death, the sons collect כתובת בנין דכרין, and one כתובה can count as the surplus for the other. The גמרא explains why both parts of his ruling are needed: we do not worry that the heirs will quarrel. A new משנה follows. If the estate covers only the two כתובות, all the sons split it equally. With one extra דינר, each family takes its mother's כתובה. בית דין sets the value, and future property does not count. רבי שמעון holds that only land counts. The גמרא then asks what happens if the estate grew after the father died. It brings the case of בר צרצור, which went from רב עמרם to רב נחמן, whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First suggestion: they argue about whether the extra דינר can be movable property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that the תנא קמא requires the extra דינר to be in קרקע, while רבי שמעון accepts even מטלטלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they disagree about a דינר of land. One master holds: land, yes; movable items, no. The other master holds: even movable items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way to explain the difference between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון in the ברייתא. It says the argument is about what kind of property the extra דינר must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that there must be one extra דינר. The suggested argument is about its form. The תנא קמא counts the surplus only if it is in קרקע, while רבי שמעון counts it even if it is in מטלטלין.
steps.confusionAlert: The first 'מר סבר' here is the תנא קמא, the stricter view that requires land. The second 'מר סבר' is רבי שמעון, the more lenient view in this suggestion.

phrases.english: And here they disagree about a dinar of land.
One master holds: land — yes,
movable items — no.
And the other master holds: even movable items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about what separates the תנא קמא from רבי שמעון in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two opinions seem to say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: They differ over whether the surplus דינר may be in מטלטלין.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: רבי שמעון says movable property counts for nothing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה quotes רבי שמעון saying that נכסים שאין להם אחריות do not count, and that the surplus must be in land. So he cannot be the one who accepts מטלטלין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say this? But we learned in the משנה: רבי שמעון says, even if there is property that is not a guarantee, it is worth nothing, unless there is property that is a guarantee, more than the two כתובות by a דינר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the first suggestion. Our own משנה shows that רבי שמעון requires the extra דינר to be in land, not movable property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first suggestion made רבי שמעון the lenient one about מטלטלין. The משנה says the opposite: for רבי שמעון, נכסים שאין להם אחריות (movables) are 'nothing', and only נכסים שיש להם אחריות (land) count toward the extra דינר. So the suggestion contradicts a clear statement of רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
Property that is not a guarantee, meaning movables
Property that is a guarantee, meaning land
They are nothing, they do not count

phrases.english: But can you say this?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if there is property
that has no guarantee, it is nothing,
phrases.notes: 'No guarantee' means movable property, which a lender cannot collect from once it is sold.

phrases.english: unless there is property
that has a guarantee,
exceeding the two marriage contracts by a dinar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 1 by quoting the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי שמעון accepts a surplus in מטלטלין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly has רבי שמעון saying movables count for nothing and only land counts.

steps.title: Second suggestion: they argue about whether the extra דינר can be sold, liened land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests the תנא קמא counts the surplus only from נכסים בני חורין, while רבי שמעון counts it even from נכסים משועבדים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, here they disagree about a דינר of liened property. One master holds: from free property, yes; from liened property, no. The other master holds: even from liened property.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first idea failed, the גמרא proposes a new point of dispute. Both agree the surplus must be land, but they argue whether land that was already sold to buyers (משועבדים) counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps רבי שמעון's rule from the משנה that only land counts. The new dispute is about land the father sold, which is still liened to the debt. The תנא קמא requires the extra דינר in free, unsold land (בני חורין). רבי שמעון counts it even in liened land.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, introducing a new answer after the first one failed
Liened property, land sold to buyers but still tied to earlier debts
Free property, land still in the estate and not sold

phrases.english: Rather, here they disagree about a dinar of liened property.
One master holds: from free property — yes,
from liened property — no,
and the other master holds: even from liened property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected suggestion of step 1 after the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about movables versus land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both require land. The dispute is about free land versus liened land.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי שמעון's wording: 'if there is' should be 'since there is'
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון is the lenient one who counts liened land, his wording 'if there is a surplus' sounds like a condition. He should have said 'since there is a surplus'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, רבי שמעון says 'if there is a surplus of a דינר.' He should have said 'since there is a surplus of a דינר'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second suggestion from the exact words of the ברייתא. רבי שמעון's phrasing does not match the role this suggestion gives him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 3, in the case discussed a surplus already exists in liened land, and רבי שמעון comes to say it counts. Then he should say 'since there is a surplus', stating a fact. 'If there is' sounds like he is setting a condition that may not be met, which does not fit a lenient addition.

phrases.english: If so, Rabbi Shimon says:
"If there is a surplus of a dinar" —

phrases.aramaic: ״כֵּיוָן שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם מוֹתַר דִּינָר״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!
phrases.english: he should have said "since there is a surplus of a dinar"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second suggestion from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי שמעון counts a surplus even in liened land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lenient view about an existing surplus should be worded 'since there is', not the conditional 'if there is'.

steps.title: A new explanation: they argue about less than a dinar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier explanations and suggests the מחלוקת is about whether a surplus smaller than a dinar is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they argue about less than a dinar. One opinion holds that a dinar counts and less than a dinar does not. The other holds that even less than a dinar counts.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the explanation in Step 3 was just knocked down, the גמרא tries a completely new way to explain what the two sides argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the argument is about the size of the surplus, not the type of property. One side needs a full dinar of extra money. The other side accepts any extra amount, even less than a dinar.

phrases.english: Rather, they argue about less than a dinar:
One Sage holds: a dinar, yes,
less than a dinar, no,
and the other Sage holds: even less than a dinar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation from Step 3, which Step 4 knocked down
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the point of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument was about the type of property (land or מטלטלין, free or liened)
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about how big the surplus must be: a full dinar or even less

steps.title: But רבי שמעון mentions a dinar
steps.stepSummary: The new explanation can't fit רבי שמעון as the lenient one, because his own words say 'a dinar'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון said 'a dinar'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from Step 5. רבי שמעון cannot be the one who accepts less than a dinar, because he himself speaks of a dinar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 made רבי שמעון the lenient one who accepts even less than a dinar. But his words in the source set a dinar as the amount. So he cannot hold that less is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: but look, isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But רבי שמעון says "a dinar"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of Step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: Calling רבי שמעון the one who accepts less than a dinar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own words mention a dinar, so he must require a full dinar

steps.title: Flipping the opinions doesn't work either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers reversing who holds what, and rejects it because the תנא קמא of the משנה also says a dinar.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: reverse the opinions. But the תנא קמא of our משנה also said a dinar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a possible fix (swap the two opinions) and shuts it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we swap, the תנא קמא becomes the one who accepts less than a dinar. But the תנא קמא in the משנה clearly speaks of a dinar too. So nobody can be the lenient side, and the 'less than a dinar' explanation falls apart completely.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a real answer from the גמרא. It is a suggested fix that the גמרא raises only to reject it in the same breath.

phrases.english: And if you would say: reverse,
phrases.notes: He means: swap them, so the תנא קמא accepts less than a dinar and רבי שמעון needs a full dinar.

phrases.english: the first Tanna of our משנה
also says a dinar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and rejects a possible defense against the challenge of Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea of swapping the opinions inside the 'less than a dinar' explanation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תנא קמא of the משנה also requires a dinar, so he can't be the lenient side either

steps.title: Back to the first two explanations, with the opinions flipped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the מחלוקת is like the first two explanations (type of property), but the opinions are swapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like those first two versions, and reverse the opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question. It returns to the explanations from Steps 1 and 3 and fixes their problems by swapping who holds which opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier explanations failed only because רבי שמעון was made the lenient one, while his words show he is strict. Once we swap, the תנא קמא is lenient (surplus counts even in מטלטלין or liened land) and רבי שמעון is strict (he needs a dinar of free land). Now the challenges from Steps 2 and 4 no longer apply.

keyTerms.meaning: two versions, two ways of explaining

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: the תנא קמא counts the surplus even from מטלטלין or liened property. רבי שמעון needs the surplus to be a dinar of free land.

phrases.english: Rather, like those
first two versions
phrases.notes: These are the explanations from Steps 1 and 3: land versus מטלטלין, and free versus liened property.

phrases.english: and reverse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי הָנָךְ תְּרֵי לִישָּׁנֵאי קַמָּאֵי וְאֵיפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the 'less than a dinar' explanation fails, returns to the earlier explanations and fixes them
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת is about the type of property. The תנא קמא is lenient and רבי שמעון is strict.

steps.title: The הלכה of מר זוטרא in the name of רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה: when one wife died during the husband's life and one after his death, the sons collect כתובת בנין דכרין, and one כתובה can count as the extra amount for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא: The הלכה is that when one wife died in his lifetime and one at his death, they get כתובת בנין דכרין, and one כתובה becomes the surplus for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: After the debate about how to explain the opinions, the גמרא gives the practical ruling for this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things are ruled. First, the sons of the wife who died during the husband's life still collect כתובת בנין דכרין, even though the other wife outlived him. Second, the other wife's כתובה can be counted as the extra amount the estate needs, so the sons can collect.

keyTerms.meaning: the right of a wife's sons to inherit her כתובה from their father's estate
surplus, the extra amount left over

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole sugya about two wives dying at different times.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה: the sons collect כתובת בנין דכרין even in the case of one wife dying in his lifetime and one after, and one כתובה can count as the surplus for the other.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: מר זוטרא said in the name of רב פפא:
The הלכה is: one in his lifetime and one at his death
phrases.notes: One wife died while the husband was alive, and the other died after him.

phrases.english: they have כתובת בנין דכרין,
and a כתובה becomes the surplus for the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב פָּפָּא, הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the explanations are settled, gives the practical ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of one wife dying in his lifetime and one after his death, the sons collect כתובת בנין דכרין, and one כתובה counts as the surplus for the other
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כתובת בנין דכרין applies in this case, and a כתובה can serve as the needed surplus.

steps.title: Why does מר זוטרא need to say both rulings?
steps.stepSummary: The first ruling alone is not enough, but the second ruling seems to include the first, so why say the first at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine: if he had taught us only that sons collect when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, I would think they collect only when a real extra dinar is left over. But let him teach us only that one כתובה counts as the extra for the other. From that I would already know that sons collect in the case of one wife in his lifetime and one after his death!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why מר זוטרא had to say both parts of his ruling. The second part seems to already include the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'בשלמא' half grants that the second ruling adds something: without it, we would still need a real extra dinar. But the 'אלא' half pushes back. The second ruling only makes sense if sons collect in this mixed case, so the first ruling seems unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / fine. This opens the part of the question that is not a problem.
I would have said. This is what we would wrongly think without the teaching.
The rule that a wife's sons inherit her כתובה money from their father's estate
An extra dinar left in the estate after the כתובות are paid, needed so the regular inheritance is not wiped out

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question on the הלכה itself. The הלכה was already settled in the previous step. The גמרא is only asking why it needed to be said in two parts.

phrases.english: Granted, if he had taught us
that when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death
they have כתובת בנין דכרין
and had not taught us
that one כתובה becomes the extra amount for the other
I would have said:
if there is an extra dinar, yes,
if not, no.
But let him teach us only
that one כתובה becomes the extra amount for the other,
and I would know on my own
that because, when one died in his lifetime and one after his death,
they have כתובת בנין דכרין!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the two-part הלכה stated in step 9 needs both parts
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the first half of מר זוטרא's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second half seems to include the first half, so the first half looks unneeded

steps.title: Without the first ruling, we might limit it to a case with three wives
steps.stepSummary: With only the second ruling, we might think it applies only where the wife who died later had just a daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had taught us only that, I would have said it applies in a case where he married three wives, and two died in his lifetime and one after his death. And the one who died after his death had a daughter, and a daughter is not an heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer. It shows how we might read the second ruling too narrowly if it stood alone. The next line finishes the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, 'one כתובה counts as the extra for the other' could fit a case with three wives. The two wives who died in his lifetime both have sons collecting. The wife who died after him left only a daughter, who does not inherit. In that case no rival son would complain, so we could not learn from it about a case where a son is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: For example / such as. It narrows the ruling to a specific case.
She gave birth to a girl
Someone who inherits. A daughter does not inherit when there are sons.

phrases.english: If he had taught us only that,
phrases.notes: 'That' means only the second ruling, that one כתובה can count as the extra for the other.

phrases.english: I would have said:
it means a case where he married three wives,
and two died in his lifetime and one after his death.
And that one who died after his death
had given birth to a daughter,
and a daughter is not an heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering the question of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the second ruling alone could be read as covering only a narrow case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second ruling applies only to three wives, where the last wife left just a daughter
steps.terutzMaskana: Finished in the next step: the first ruling is needed to cover the case where a son is involved

steps.title: We do not worry that the heirs will quarrel
steps.stepSummary: Where the wife who died later had a son, we might fear fighting between heirs. Saying both rulings teaches that we do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when one wife died in his lifetime and one after his death, and the one who died after his death had a son, you might say we should worry about quarreling. So he teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The first ruling is needed to teach that even when a son of the other wife is involved, the rule still holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two wives where the later one had a son, there is a son on each side. We might fear the brothers would fight over the money and say the rule should not apply. By stating the two-wife case outright, מר זוטרא teaches that this fear does not stop the rule, and both parts of his statement are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: We should worry about / take into account
He is teaching us. This shows what new point the statement adds.

steps.whatToRemember: Both parts of מר זוטרא's הלכה are needed. Without the second, we would need a real extra dinar. Without the first, we might limit the rule to cases with no risk of fighting. The bottom line is that we do not worry about the heirs quarreling.

phrases.english: But when one died in his lifetime and one after his death,
and the one who died after his death
had given birth to a son
I might say we should worry about quarreling,
so he teaches us that we do not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא לֵיחוּשׁ לְאִינְּצוֹיֵי, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer begun in step 11 and settles the question of step 10
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both halves of מר זוטרא's statement are needed. The rule applies even where a son of the other wife is involved, and we do not worry about quarreling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining why both parts of the statement are needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the second ruling, we might think it applies only where no son of the later wife could quarrel. Where the later wife had a son, we would worry about אינצויי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ruling is stated to teach that even in the two-wife case where the later wife had a son, we do not worry about quarreling. So both parts are needed.

steps.title: Only enough for two כתובות: the sons split equally
steps.stepSummary: A man had two wives who both died before him, and then he died. If the estate covers only the two כתובות, the sons do not collect their mothers' כתובות. They divide the estate equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man was married to two women. They died, and then he died. The orphans want their mother's כתובה, but there is only enough for the two כתובות. In that case they divide equally.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets up the case of two wives who died before their husband, and gives its first rule: if the estate covers only the two כתובות, everyone splits equally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, sons may collect their own mother's כתובה from their father's estate. This is called כתובת בנין דכרין. Here that right does not apply, because the two כתובות would use up the whole estate. So the sons inherit the regular way, splitting equally among all the brothers.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
The right of a wife's sons to collect her כתובה from their father's estate.
Orphans. Here, the sons of the two wives.
They divide equally, as in a normal Torah inheritance.

steps.confusionAlert: Equal division here is not between the two wives' families. It is among all the sons equally, the regular inheritance way. Each family does not get its own mother's כתובה amount.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who was married to two women,
and they died, and afterward he died,
and the orphans seek their mother's כתובה,
but there is only enough there for two כתובות,
they divide equally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It moves on from the previous discussion of כתובת בנין דכרין to the case where both wives died before the husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the estate covers only the two כתובות, כתובת בנין דכרין is not collected. All the sons split the estate equally.

steps.title: An extra דינר left over: each set of sons takes its mother's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: If even one דינר is left beyond the two כתובות, each group of sons collects its own mother's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was one extra דינר there, these sons take their mother's כתובה, and those sons take their mother's כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its second rule. If even a tiny surplus of one דינר exists, כתובת בנין דכרין does apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change from the last step is that a small amount is left over. Because something remains to be inherited the regular way, each family can take its mother's כתובה first. The leftover is then split normally.

keyTerms.meaning: A surplus of one דינר beyond the two כתובות.

steps.whyThisMatters: This extra-דינר requirement is the key point of the whole משנה. The next two rules both deal with what counts toward that דינר.

phrases.english: If there was a surplus of a דינר there,
these take their mother's כתובה,
and those take their mother's כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 13: an extra דינר is left over.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a surplus of even one דינר, each group of sons collects its own mother's כתובה.

steps.title: The sons cannot raise the value themselves; בית דין appraises
steps.stepSummary: The sons may offer to value the property higher so an extra דינר appears. We do not listen to them. בית דין appraises the property.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the orphans say, 'We will value our father's property one דינר higher so that we can take our mother's כתובה,' we do not listen to them. Instead, the property is appraised in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third rule. The sons cannot invent the extra דינר by agreeing to an inflated value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some sons might want the extra דינר to exist, so they offer to count the property as worth more than it really is. The משנה says the value is not up to them. בית דין sets the real value, and only a real surplus counts.

keyTerms.meaning: We raise. Here it means valuing the property higher.
We do not listen to them.
They appraise, or estimate the value.

phrases.english: If the orphans said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנַחְנוּ מַעֲלִים עַל נִכְסֵי אָבִינוּ יָפֶה דִּינָר
phrases.english: We will raise the value of our father's property by a דינר,
phrases.notes: They mean they will accept their share at a higher price than it is really worth. That would leave a דינר over.

phrases.english: so that they can take their mother's כתובה,
we do not listen to them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׁמִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: rather, the property is appraised in בית דין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָמְרוּ יְתוֹמִים אֲנַחְנוּ מַעֲלִים עַל נִכְסֵי אָבִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines how the extra דינר from step 14 is measured: by בית דין, not by the sons' offer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The extra דינר must be real, based on בית דין's appraisal. The sons cannot create it by agreeing to a higher value.

steps.title: Property only expected later does not count
steps.stepSummary: Property the estate is only due to receive in the future does not count as part of the estate when checking for the extra דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was property that is only expected to come, it does not count like property already held.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with its fourth rule. Only property the estate already holds counts toward the extra דינר, not property it may receive later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the estate is owed something that has not arrived yet. If that were counted, there might be an extra דינר. The משנה says such future property is not treated like property already in hand, so it cannot create the surplus.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that is due to come in the future but is not yet held.
Property already held, in the estate's possession.

steps.whatToRemember: כתובת בנין דכרין is collected only when a real surplus of at least one דינר exists. בית דין sets the value, and only property already held counts. Property that is only expected later does not.

phrases.english: If there was property there that is only expected to come,
phrases.notes: This is property the estate is owed but has not yet received.

phrases.english: it is not like property already held.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further defines what counts toward the extra דינר: future property does not.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property the estate expects to receive later is not counted when checking for the extra דינר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: Only land counts toward the extra dinar
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that movable property does not count. The extra דינר must come from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: Even if the estate has movable property, it does not count at all. The sons collect their mothers' כתובות only if there is land worth at least one דינר more than the two כתובות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the משנה. רבי שמעון adds a limit: only land counts when we check whether one extra דינר is left over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only asked whether one extra דינר was left beyond the two כתובות. רבי שמעון narrows this. Movable things do not help at all. The extra must be in land, the kind of property that backs up a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that does not back up a loan, meaning movable things
Property that backs up a loan, meaning land

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Even if there is property there
that does not serve as a guarantee,
phrases.notes: This means movable things, not land. Land is what backs up a loan.

phrases.english: it counts for nothing,
unless there is property there
that serves as a guarantee (land)
worth one dinar more than the two marriage contracts.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ שָׁם נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further limit on what counts as part of the estate, after the limit on future property in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only land counts toward the extra דינר. Movable property does not count at all.

steps.title: ברייתא: The rule holds even when the two marriage contracts differ in size
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches a case where one כתובה is 1000 and the other is 500. If one extra דינר is left, each group of sons takes its mother's כתובה. If not, they split the estate equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: One wife's כתובה was 1000 and the other's was 500. If one extra דינר is left, these sons take their mother's כתובה and those sons take their mother's כתובה. If not, they divide everything equally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It brings a ברייתא that applies the extra-דינר rule to two כתובות of different sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With unequal כתובות, the sons of the 1000 wife gain a lot if the כתובות are paid out. Without the extra דינר, though, they get nothing special. Everyone splits the estate equally, just like any inheritance.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: Equal division here means the brothers split the estate as ordinary heirs. It does not mean they split the two כתובות.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
This one had a thousand and that one five hundred,
if there is an extra dinar there,
these sons take their mother's marriage contract
and those sons take their mother's marriage contract.
And if not, they divide equally.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לָזוֹ אֶלֶף וְלָזוֹ חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא. It shows the משנה's rule from steps 13 and 14 applied to unequal כתובות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with unequal כתובות, each group collects its mother's כתובה only if one extra דינר is left. Otherwise they divide equally.

steps.title: Obvious case: The estate was large at death and later shrank
steps.stepSummary: The extra דינר existed at the father's death, but the property lost value later. The sons already earned their mothers' כתובות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious: if the property was large and then got smaller, the heirs already acquired their rights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a case it calls obvious. This sets up the harder question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is the situation at the moment of the father's death. If the extra דינר existed then, the sons' right to their mothers' כתובות was locked in. A later drop in value does not take it away.

keyTerms.meaning: Many, and then reduced (the estate shrank)

phrases.english: It is obvious: if the property was large and became small,
phrases.notes: "Large" means there was an extra דינר when the father died. Then the value went down.

phrases.english: the heirs already acquired them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the basic rule to the question of timing: when do we check for the extra דינר?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the extra דינר existed at the father's death, the sons' rights to their mothers' כתובות are fixed, even if the estate later shrinks.

steps.title: Question: What if the estate was small at death and later grew?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the reverse case. There was no extra דינר at the father's death, but the property rose in value before the brothers divided it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the property was small and then grew, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question. This is the opposite of the obvious case in step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here no right existed at the time of death, but by the time of dividing there is an extra דינר. The question is which moment counts: the death or the division.

keyTerms.meaning: Few, and then increased (the estate grew)

phrases.english: If the property was small and then grew, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the obvious case in step 19 as a contrast to ask about the unclear reverse case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the sons collect their mothers' כתובות when the extra דינר appears only after the father's death, because the property went up in value?

steps.title: The case of בר צרצור's estate before רב עמרם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a real case to answer the question. בר צרצור's estate was small and then grew. רב עמרם told the sons to make peace, and they ignored him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The estate of בר צרצור was small and then grew. The sons came before רב עמרם. He told them: Go make peace with them. They did not listen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an attempted proof from a real case that matches the question. The story continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The estate went from small to large, exactly the case in question. רב עמרם did not give a clear ruling. Instead he told one side to calm the other side down. This hints that he was unsure. The sons refused, so the case is not settled yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (it brings a source to answer a question)
Make peace with them, appease them

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For the property of the house of bar Tzartzur
was small and then grew,
and they came before Rav Amram.
He said to them: Go, appease them.
phrases.notes: He is talking to the sons of the wife with the bigger כתובה. He tells them to make peace with the other brothers.

phrases.english: They paid no attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּנִיכְסֵי דְּבֵי בַּר צַרְצוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question in step 20 with a real case that matches it exactly.
steps.raayaObject: Whether property that grew after the father's death counts toward the extra דינר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of בר צרצור's estate, brought before רב עמרם

steps.title: רב עמרם threatens the brothers who refuse to make peace
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם warns the sons that if they do not appease the other side, he will strike them with a 'thorn that does not draw blood.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If you do not make peace with them, I will strike you with a thorn that does not draw blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of בר צרצור continues. רב עמרם gets tough with the sons who ignored his call to make peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עמרם does not give a clear legal ruling. He pushes for a compromise, and the 'thorn that does not draw blood' is a threat of נידוי (excommunication), not a physical blow. This hints that he saw the question as unclear and preferred that the brothers settle it themselves.
steps.confusionAlert: רב עמרם is not threatening to hit anyone. The 'bloodless thorn' means a ban of נידוי.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי לָא מְפַיְּיסִיתוּ לְהוּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: If you do not appease them,
I will strike you with a thorn
that does not draw blood.
phrases.notes: A thorn that hurts without drawing blood is a way of saying he will put them in נידוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי לָא מְפַיְּיסִיתוּ לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of בר צרצור that was brought as evidence in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The question from step 20: does value gained after the father's death create the extra דינר?
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב עמרם's response in the real case of בר צרצור. He pushes for a compromise instead of ruling, which suggests the law was unclear to him.

steps.title: רב נחמן begins his ruling by comparing it to property that lost value
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם sends the case to רב נחמן. רב נחמן starts his answer with 'just as' property that was large and then shrank...
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent them before רב נחמן. רב נחמן said to them: Just as when the property was abundant and then shrank...
steps.whatsHappening: The case moves to a higher authority, רב נחמן. He begins a comparison, and the second half of his sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן opens with the case from step 19: there was an extra דינר at the father's death, and the property shrank later. In that case the sons keep their mothers' כתובות because they gained them at the father's death. His words 'just as' show he will judge the reverse case the same way, by what existed at the time of death.

keyTerms.meaning: abundant and then decreased in value

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key principle for the case of rising value: what counts is the state of the estate when the father died.

phrases.english: He sent them before Rav Nachman.
He said to them:
Just as when they were abundant and then decreased,
phrases.notes: This points back to step 19, where the estate had an extra דינר when the father died but lost value later. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁדְּרִינְהוּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לָהֶן: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּרוּבִּין וְנִתְמַעֲטוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story moves from רב עמרם, who only pushed for a compromise, to רב נחמן, who begins to give a ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does property that grew in value after the father's death, before the brothers divided it, create the extra דינר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not finished yet. רב נחמן begins by comparing the case to property that shrank after the father's death (step 19), which shows the time of death will decide.
